title: Verification Playbook Library
summary: Thirty procedural playbooks turn the Phase 116 conversion-stage, claim-type, and quality contracts into repeatable reviewer decisions with direct-evidence thresholds, rejection tests, worked examples, correction paths, and stop rules.
publication_boundary: This library explains how to review existing evidence. It creates no source, signal, gate decision, receipt, observation, outcome, score, ranking, or automatic publication authority.
operating_rules: A checklist organizes human review; it does not make a publication decision.
Every worked example inherits the status, scope, source lineage, and limitations of its cited Published signal.
A failed checklist or inadmissible substitution stops the claim at its last directly established state.
Correction requires visible prior and current states plus complete downstream propagation.

stage_playbooks.title: Verify a named context or baseline
stage_playbooks.canonical_definition: Is the named entity and its current evidence boundary established?
stage_playbooks.what_it_can_establish: A bounded starting state for one named entity, cohort, asset, service area, or population at a stated date or period. The decision may establish what is known before conversion begins, but never that a later event occurred.
minimum_direct_evidence: A primary record that names the entity or cohort and the responsible reporting authority.
A dated observation period with a defined measure, unit, denominator, and geographic boundary.
A reconciliation note for aliases, entity changes, missing values, and series breaks.
false_positives: A market forecast described in present tense.
A national statistic applied to an unnamed local project.
Nameplate capacity treated as available or qualified capacity.
inadmissible_substitutions: A press release without the underlying table or register.
An undated dashboard screenshot with no extractable period.
A nearby facility or parent-company total substituted for the named entity.
reviewer_checklist: Resolve the canonical entity ID before reading the value.
Record the source, event, capture, and review dates separately.
Transcribe the measure, unit, denominator, exclusions, and geography.
Check whether the entity or methodology changed during the period.
Compare aliases against the canonical identity registry.
State the first downstream artifact that this baseline does not establish.

worked_example.interpretation: The Maricopa record names the county, quarter, covered-employment measure, and wage context, so it supports a bounded labor baseline without proving fab readiness.

counterexample.interpretation: The MAG projection is useful scenario context, but projected regional growth cannot substitute for an observed project, workforce, or service baseline.

stage_playbooks.stop_rule: Stop at Context when the entity, period, measure, denominator, or geography cannot be resolved from a direct record; publish the ambiguity rather than choosing a convenient proxy.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior named context or baseline decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.
Propagate the correction through the source or artifact record, signal decision, canonical synthesis, pathway or mission, dependency surface, update log, and machine-readable export.
Re-run content, phase, route, and release validation before publication; a partial propagation remains unpublished.

stage_playbooks.title: Verify policy or authority
stage_playbooks.canonical_definition: Is a named policy, regulatory, permitting, or service authority established?
stage_playbooks.what_it_can_establish: A named legal, regulatory, permitting, licensing, tariff, standards, or public-process disposition, including its issuer, scope, conditions, effective date, and current status.
minimum_direct_evidence: The enacted instrument, signed order, issued permit, licence, tariff, standard, or official docket disposition.
The issuing authority's scope, effective date, conditions, expiry, appeal, and supersession fields.
An identity crosswalk connecting the instrument to the exact operator, asset, activity, or service area.
false_positives: A consultation or draft treated as adopted law.
Environmental review treated as operator authorization.
A permit application treated as an issued and effective permit.
inadmissible_substitutions: An applicant announcement instead of the regulator's disposition.
A general agency program page instead of the named instrument.
Authority for one site, operator, or activity transferred to another.
reviewer_checklist: Open the authoritative instrument, not only its landing page.
Confirm issuer competence for the exact decision.
Capture instrument number, dates, scope, conditions, and expiry.
Check amendments, appeals, stays, withdrawals, and successor instruments.
Bind the authority to the exact entity and geography.
Leave implementation, acceptance, operation, and outcome stages unchanged.

worked_example.interpretation: The FAA final rule establishes a regulatory layer for powered-lift operations while its own boundary prevents an inference that an aircraft or service has been approved or operated.

counterexample.interpretation: The LC-39A environmental decision establishes an environmental-review disposition, not every operator, vehicle, mission, construction, or operating authority required downstream.

stage_playbooks.stop_rule: Stop at Authority unless the final, current instrument and exact governed entity are both explicit; conditions and expiry remain part of the decision rather than footnotes.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior policy or authority decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.
Propagate the correction through the source or artifact record, signal decision, canonical synthesis, pathway or mission, dependency surface, update log, and machine-readable export.
Re-run content, phase, route, and release validation before publication; a partial propagation remains unpublished.

stage_playbooks.title: Verify finance, procurement, or agreement
stage_playbooks.canonical_definition: Is a named financial close, order, procurement, contract, or delivery agreement established?
stage_playbooks.what_it_can_establish: A binding or formally recorded commitment by named parties, such as financial close, appropriation, award, order, contract, offtake, grant, or delivery agreement, with conditions and scope intact.
minimum_direct_evidence: A signed agreement, executed financing notice, award instrument, order, appropriation, or official procurement record.
Named parties, committed amount or quantity where public, scope, date, conditions precedent, and termination status.
A project-identity link distinguishing selection, negotiation, execution, disbursement, and expenditure.
false_positives: A project selection described as a closed award.
A maximum contract ceiling described as money spent.
A memorandum of understanding described as an unconditional delivery obligation.
inadmissible_substitutions: A beneficiary press release without the executed instrument.
A portfolio total substituted for the named project commitment.
A forecast capital requirement substituted for secured finance.
reviewer_checklist: Classify the instrument before describing the commitment.
Name every obligated party and the receiving project.
Separate authorized, obligated, disbursed, and expended amounts.
Record conditions, milestones, cancellation rights, and expiry.
Check whether scope or counterparties changed after announcement.
Keep construction, delivery, acceptance, and outcome unestablished.

worked_example.interpretation: The official loan close establishes a named financing event for Thacker Pass; it does not establish construction completion, qualified material, shipment, or recurring supply.

counterexample.interpretation: DOE's nineteen selections open award trails, but selection alone is not an executed award, financial close, disbursement, or completed facility.

stage_playbooks.stop_rule: Stop at Commitment when execution, parties, scope, or conditions cannot be verified directly; never promote a selection, target, ceiling, or negotiation into a binding commitment.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior finance, procurement, or agreement decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.
Propagate the correction through the source or artifact record, signal decision, canonical synthesis, pathway or mission, dependency surface, update log, and machine-readable export.
Re-run content, phase, route, and release validation before publication; a partial propagation remains unpublished.

stage_playbooks.title: Verify build or implementation
stage_playbooks.canonical_definition: Is physical construction or system implementation established at the named entity?
stage_playbooks.what_it_can_establish: A dated physical or organizational implementation milestone for the exact project, asset, system, site, cohort, or migration scope, including completed scope and remaining work.
minimum_direct_evidence: A construction, installation, migration, delivery, inspection, or implementation record tied to the named entity.
A milestone definition, observed date, completed quantity or share, denominator, and remaining scope.
Evidence that distinguishes mobilization, work in progress, substantial completion, and final completion.
false_positives: A groundbreaking treated as substantial completion.
Equipment delivery treated as installed and commissioned capacity.
Portfolio progress transferred to an individual project.
inadmissible_substitutions: A rendering or future schedule instead of an observed milestone.
Contractor marketing without an owner or authority record.
Expenditure percentage substituted for physical completion.
reviewer_checklist: Resolve the project, site, asset, and package identity.
Define the milestone in physical or organizational terms.
Record completed quantity and total applicable scope.
Separate owner report, contractor report, and independent inspection.
List incomplete packages, exceptions, and dependencies.
Do not advance validation, acceptance, recurring operation, or outcome.

worked_example.interpretation: The Fab 3 topping-out record establishes a specific structural milestone at a named facility while leaving fit-out, utilities, qualification, acceptance, and production open.

counterexample.interpretation: A preliminary capital program identifies planned wastewater work, but a budget line and schedule do not establish that the assets were built, inspected, or operating.

stage_playbooks.stop_rule: Stop at the exact observed milestone. If scope, denominator, or remaining work is absent, describe the record as partial implementation evidence rather than completion.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior build or implementation decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.
Propagate the correction through the source or artifact record, signal decision, canonical synthesis, pathway or mission, dependency surface, update log, and machine-readable export.
Re-run content, phase, route, and release validation before publication; a partial propagation remains unpublished.

stage_playbooks.title: Verify test, compliance, or qualification
stage_playbooks.canonical_definition: Is named testing, inspection, compliance, qualification, or corrective action established?
stage_playbooks.what_it_can_establish: A named test, inspection, compliance, certification, qualification, or corrective-action disposition for a defined article, system, cohort, facility, or operating configuration.
minimum_direct_evidence: A test report, inspection record, certification, regulator finding, qualification lot, or corrective-action closure.
Named article or cohort, configuration, method, criteria, result, exceptions, reviewer, and decision date.
A disposition explaining failures, waivers, retests, corrective actions, and the scope of any pass.
false_positives: Participation in a pilot treated as passing its evaluation.
One laboratory result generalized to an operating fleet.
Corrective action opened treated as verified closed.
inadmissible_substitutions: A vendor performance claim without protocol or criteria.
A certification framework substituted for a product certificate.
A successful demonstration substituted for qualification under receiving-system conditions.
reviewer_checklist: Name the test article, configuration, cohort, and environment.
Capture protocol, thresholds, evaluator, and authority.
Separate measured result from interpretation and disposition.
Record exceptions, waivers, failures, and retest status.
Check transfer limits between test and operating configurations.
Keep receiving-party acceptance and sustained operation separate.

worked_example.interpretation: DARPA's published measured results identify teams, scored runs, lift ratios, and prize decisions, supporting a bounded field-test result rather than an operational-aircraft claim.

counterexample.interpretation: ARIA's multi-level pilot establishes that an evaluation occurred; it cannot by itself establish authorization, continuous assurance, accepted deployment, or mission benefit for a named system.

stage_playbooks.stop_rule: Stop at the tested configuration and stated disposition. Never extend a pass beyond the article, criteria, environment, authority, or exceptions recorded.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior test, compliance, or qualification decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.
Propagate the correction through the source or artifact record, signal decision, canonical synthesis, pathway or mission, dependency surface, update log, and machine-readable export.
Re-run content, phase, route, and release validation before publication; a partial propagation remains unpublished.

stage_playbooks.title: Verify accepted service, product, or cutover
stage_playbooks.canonical_definition: Has a named receiving authority or customer accepted the asset, service, product, or transition?
stage_playbooks.what_it_can_establish: A formal receiving-party decision that a named asset, service, product, lot, handover, or system transition satisfies stated acceptance criteria for a bounded operational scope.
minimum_direct_evidence: A signed acceptance, handover, turnover, authority-to-use, customer receipt, closeout, or cutover record.
Named receiver, accepted object, criteria, date, exceptions, warranty or punch-list status, and authorized scope.
A link from acceptance to the exact delivered configuration, lot, station, facility, or system.
false_positives: Substantial completion treated as final acceptance.
A vendor shipment treated as customer receipt.
Permission to operate treated as receiver acceptance.
inadmissible_substitutions: A construction progress report without receiving-party signoff.
An aggregate delivery count without named accepted assets.
A target in-service date substituted for a dated acceptance record.
reviewer_checklist: Identify the receiving party and its authority to accept.
Resolve the accepted object and configuration exactly.
Transcribe criteria, decision date, scope, and exceptions.
Separate conditional, partial, provisional, and final acceptance.
Record punch-list, warranty, closeout, and rejected-scope status.
Do not infer repeated use, reliability, utilization, or outcome.

worked_example.interpretation: Amtrak's turnover of eleven named station projects for passenger use is stronger receiving-system evidence than construction progress, while still not establishing recurring reliability or portfolio-wide outcomes.

counterexample.interpretation: A portfolio substantial-completion count does not identify final acceptance, passenger use, exceptions, or closeout for every station in its denominator.

stage_playbooks.stop_rule: Stop before Acceptance unless the receiver, accepted object, criteria, decision, and exceptions are explicit. Partial or conditional acceptance must retain that qualifier everywhere.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior accepted service, product, or cutover decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.
Propagate the correction through the source or artifact record, signal decision, canonical synthesis, pathway or mission, dependency surface, update log, and machine-readable export.
Re-run content, phase, route, and release validation before publication; a partial propagation remains unpublished.

stage_playbooks.title: Verify recurring operation or output
stage_playbooks.canonical_definition: Is compatible recurring service, operation, or output established?
stage_playbooks.what_it_can_establish: Repeated service, use, adoption, dispatch, production, or output for one stable entity or cohort across compatible periods, including outages, attrition, and denominator changes.
minimum_direct_evidence: At least two compatible operating observations for the same named asset, service, facility, or cohort.
Stable period, unit, denominator, coverage, outage, attrition, and exception definitions.
A reconciliation of maintenance, downtime, curtailment, cancellations, revisions, and identity changes.
false_positives: One successful run described as sustained operation.
Installed capacity described as recurring output.
Cumulative totals with no period or exposure denominator described as reliability.
inadmissible_substitutions: A capacity plate or commissioning certificate instead of operating records.
Provider-wide totals substituted for a fixed eligible cohort.
Two observations with incompatible units or entity boundaries.
reviewer_checklist: Lock the entity and cohort identity across periods.
Require at least two comparable operating intervals.
Reconcile units, denominators, outages, and missing periods.
Separate availability, utilization, output, quality, and adoption.
Inspect revisions and series breaks before calculating change.
Keep causal and net-public-outcome claims outside this decision.

worked_example.interpretation: The named monthly Manatee operating record supports a bounded operation reading because it adds period-specific activity beyond nameplate capacity.

counterexample.interpretation: The repeated 409 MW nameplate figure is a stable capacity description, not proof that the battery dispatched, remained available, or delivered recurring service.

stage_playbooks.stop_rule: Stop at Acceptance or a single operation when repeated compatible periods are absent. Do not manufacture recurrence by combining incomparable records.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior recurring operation or output decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.
Propagate the correction through the source or artifact record, signal decision, canonical synthesis, pathway or mission, dependency surface, update log, and machine-readable export.
Re-run content, phase, route, and release validation before publication; a partial propagation remains unpublished.

stage_playbooks.title: Verify a comparable outcome
stage_playbooks.canonical_definition: Is a repeated outcome series established with stable identity, period, definition, and denominator?
stage_playbooks.what_it_can_establish: A repeated change in a defined service, welfare, cost, safety, reliability, environmental, resilience, or mission measure for a stable population or system, with comparison and attribution limits stated.
minimum_direct_evidence: A repeated outcome series with stable identity, measure, unit, period, denominator, exclusions, and revision policy.
A declared comparison design or bounded before-after reading with uncertainty and alternative explanations.
Exposure, service, or operating context sufficient to distinguish outcome from activity volume.
false_positives: A regulatory approval described as safety improvement.
A single favorable event described as a trend or causal effect.
inadmissible_substitutions: Testimonials or anecdotes instead of a defined series.
Incompatible geographies or denominators ranked together.
Modeled benefits substituted for observed outcomes.
reviewer_checklist: Define the outcome independently of the intervention claim.
Lock entity, population, period, unit, and denominator.
Require repeated compatible observations and disclose revisions.
Document exposure, confounders, uncertainty, and counterevidence.
Test whether the comparison survives series-break exclusions.
State what association, contribution, or causation is and is not supported.

worked_example.interpretation: DOT's annual carrier-service rail can support bounded multi-period service measures because the reporting series preserves a comparable unit and carrier context; causal attribution still requires separate analysis.

counterexample.interpretation: Expanded legal authority for fared driverless service does not establish a repeated safety, access, affordability, reliability, or public-benefit outcome.

stage_playbooks.stop_rule: Stop before Outcome when identity, period, definition, denominator, repeated observations, uncertainty, or comparison compatibility is missing. Inadmissibility is a valid result.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior comparable outcome decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.
Propagate the correction through the source or artifact record, signal decision, canonical synthesis, pathway or mission, dependency surface, update log, and machine-readable export.
Re-run content, phase, route, and release validation before publication; a partial propagation remains unpublished.

claim_review_protocols.title: Review a baseline or context claim
claim_review_protocols.canonical_definition: Describes a named starting condition, system boundary, inventory, demand, capacity or historical state.
claim_review_protocols.what_it_can_establish: A dated starting condition for a named population or system, without implying change.
minimum_direct_evidence: Observed primary table with entity, period, measure, and denominator.

Series and revision metadata.
false_positives: National average assigned to one place.

worked_example.interpretation: This signal supports a county-period workforce baseline with an explicit limit on fab-readiness inference.

counterexample.interpretation: A projection remains scenario context and is inadmissible as an observed baseline.

claim_review_protocols.stop_rule: Do not publish a baseline claim until subject, period, measure, and denominator all resolve.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior baseline or context decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.
Record the correcting authority, reason, decision date, prior state, current state, and every affected stable ID.

claim_review_protocols.title: Review a research-result claim
claim_review_protocols.canonical_definition: Reports a measured finding from a study, laboratory, model, field trial or evaluation.
claim_review_protocols.what_it_can_establish: A measured finding for a defined study population, test article, method, and setting, with transfer limits.
minimum_direct_evidence: Citable study or test report.
Method, population, result, uncertainty, and limitations.
Version and correction history.
false_positives: Abstract headline generalized beyond the study.

worked_example.interpretation: METIS is admissible as a shared-data infrastructure research test within its stated setting.

counterexample.interpretation: A research award establishes funding, not a measured research result.

claim_review_protocols.stop_rule: Stop at funding or protocol when no completed method-and-result artifact exists.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior research result decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.

claim_review_protocols.title: Review an announcement or plan claim
claim_review_protocols.canonical_definition: Records a stated intention, target, proposal, schedule or capacity ambition.
claim_review_protocols.what_it_can_establish: A named issuer's stated intention, target, proposal, schedule, or ambition, explicitly labeled as prospective.
minimum_direct_evidence: Issuer-authored dated announcement or plan.
Named object, proposed scale, horizon, and status.
Assumptions and update history where available.
false_positives: Planned date described as a commitment.
inadmissible_substitutions: Old plan superseded by a later version.
Industry forecast substituted for project plan.

counterexample.interpretation: A preliminary capital program cannot be written as completed procurement or construction.

claim_review_protocols.stop_rule: Never convert future tense into a completed stage; stop at the plan's explicit status.
correction_and_propagation_requirements: Preserve the prior announcement or plan decision and the direct artifact that supported it; never silently overwrite history.

claim_review_protocols.title: Review a forecast or scenario claim
claim_review_protocols.canonical_definition: Describes a modeled future, projection, range, target pathway or conditional scenario.
claim_review_protocols.what_it_can_establish: A conditional future path tied to a named model, base date, assumptions, horizon, range, and update history.
